topic: Distinguishing a source’s claim from your own conclusion
grammarFocus: 学术论证的限定、因果、对比与证据范围
title: Distinguishing a source’s claim from your own conclusion
instructions: 原创学术微训练；场景、机构与数值均为虚构模拟，不是事实报道或官方试题。先独立盲听答题，再用原句核对限定、比较与因果。短篇专项不能替代完整陌生测评。
transcript:
Tutor: Read the sentence you plan to put in your discussion section.
Noah: The study proves that giving every employee a flexible schedule will increase productivity.
Tutor: Does the source actually make that claim?
Noah: Looking again, it reports an association in three offices. The staff volunteered, and productivity was measured by completed service tickets over eight weeks.
Tutor: Then several limits disappeared in your sentence. Which ones?
Noah: The limited sites, the volunteer sample, the particular outcome measure and the short observation period. I also changed an association into proof of cause.
Tutor: Try a defensible version.
Noah: In the participating offices, flexible scheduling was associated with more completed tickets during the study period. That wording keeps the setting and measure visible.
Tutor: Can you still offer your own interpretation?
Noah: Yes, if I label it. I might suggest a longer comparison that also examines ticket quality. Completing more tickets does not necessarily mean solving problems better.
Tutor: How will you separate source and interpretation on the slide?
Noah: The first box will state what was observed and give the citation. The second will contain our interpretation and proposed next check. I will not put the stronger claim in the title after weakening it in the footnote.

questions.prompt: What change did Noah initially make to the relationship?
options: He turned association into proof of causation.
He described a measured cause as no relationship.
He removed productivity from the discussion entirely.
answers: He turned association into proof of causation.
questions.explanation: 依据原文“changed an association into proof of cause.”。正确项保持了原文的范围和关系，其余项改动了该信息。
questions.evidence: changed an association into proof of cause.

questions.prompt: What additional aspect would Noah examine next?
questions.explanation: 依据原文“also examines ticket quality.”。答案按原文填写，保留限定范围。

questions.prompt: What will distinguish the two boxes on the slide?
options: The title and an unrelated recruitment notice.
All limitations and all citations hidden together.
Observed findings and the group’s interpretation.
Two invented versions of the same source.
answers: Observed findings and the group’s interpretation.
questions.explanation: 依据原文“what was observed and give the citation.”。正确项保持了原文的范围和关系，其余项改动了该信息。
questions.evidence: what was observed and give the citation.

questions.prompt: Where must the stronger unsupported claim also be removed?
questions.explanation: 依据原文“the stronger claim in the title”。答案按原文填写，保留限定范围。
questions.evidence: the stronger claim in the title

grammar.title: 被动句准确保留动作对象
grammar.explanation: 被动结构是 be + 过去分词。使用它可把重点放在样本或处理步骤，不能省掉 be，也不要把过去分词当过去式主句。
grammar.example: The staff volunteered, and productivity was measured by completed service tickets over eight weeks.

questions.evidence: The records were checked by two assistants.

part1: What do you usually read about this topic?
Have you ever made a choice involving reporting another study accurately?
What information would help you make that choice?
Who would you ask for a different opinion?
speaking.part2: Describe a decision about reporting another study accurately. You should say what the decision was, what alternatives were available, what evidence you used, and explain what you would check before recommending it to others.
part3: Why might an output count miss quality?
Can interpretation go beyond observation if labelled?
Why should a title respect the limitations too?

transfer.writing: Write an evidence-based paragraph of 120–160 words about reporting another study accurately. State one claim, support it with a relevant example, acknowledge a limitation, and explain what further evidence would change your conclusion. Use a new example; do not copy the passage.
